text: Found while judging skills-meters/the-web-build-seeds-stance-mastery-at-1. The stance slash-length formulas DIVERGE between builds, and the 'Light x0.54' figure in circulation is mislabelled - 0.54 is HEAVY. Web v0.717 (§1t99s0§.as, switch at :3091): Light case §1t12220s0§ :3094 is a FLAT 'this.§1t4417s0§ = this.§1t4420s0§ * 1.4' with NO mastery term at all; Balanced §1t12221s0§ :3105 is '§1t4420s0§ * (1 + 0.2 * §1t4422s0§ * 0.1)' = x1.02 at mastery 1; Heavy §1t12222s0§ :3116 is '§1t4420s0§ * (0.5 + 0.4 * §1t4423s0§ * 0.1)' = x0.54 at mastery 1, floored at 100 px by :3117-3120. Android v0.682 (MCSPlayer.as setStance :3027): LIGHT :3030 'baseSlashLength * 1.5'; BALANCED :3041 '(1 + 0.5 * balancedMastery * 0.01)'; HEAVY :3052 '(0.5 + 0.5 * heavyMastery * 0.01)' floored at 100 by :3053-3056. So THREE things differ: the Light constant (1.4 web vs 1.5 android), the Balanced mastery coefficient (0.2*0.1=0.02 vs 0.5*0.01=0.005), and the Heavy coefficient (0.04 vs 0.005) - a 4x-8x difference in how much mastery buys. §1t4422s0§/§1t4423s0§ are pinned to balancedMastery/heavyMastery by MCSPlayer.as:182's named signature via the initPlayer argument bridge. There is also a fourth web case §1t12224s0§ at :3130-3131 with a flat *1.4 (android's REVERSED_STANCE, :3067, is *1.5).

lane_impact: L5 combat-core: model reach as baseSlashLength(speed) x stanceMult(mastery), floor 100 on Heavy only. The player's baseSlashLength comes from the equivalent web caller and is still unread - that is now the ONLY missing number for reach, and it is one lookup, not a measurement.
quote: EnemyElite.as:102 'var baseSlashLength:int = 120 + Math.floor(maxincrement * val / (20 + val));' with :101 'var maxincrement:int = 90;' and :100 'var val:int = xml.speed;' · web §1t99s0§.as:194 'this.§1t4420s0§ = param10;'
text: hunter-s27b/heavy-reach-has-a-hard-100px-floor records its one remaining unknown as 'the base value 1t4420s0 ... which is set elsewhere and which I did not resolve'. It resolves. Web: 1t99s0.as:105 initialises 1t4420s0 to 10, :194 assigns it from the tenth initPlayer parameter, and :223 halves it ('*= 0.5') in one branch. The android twin is positionally identical - MCSPlayer.as:107 'internal var baseSlashLength:int = 10;', :182 declares initPlayer with baseSlashLength as its tenth parameter, :193 assigns it, :222 halves it - which names 1t4420s0 = baseSlashLength. The value fed in, for NPCs, is computed by the caller: EnemyElite.as:102 baseSlashLength = 120 + floor(90 * speed / (20 + speed)), i.e. a saturating curve from 120 px at speed 0 toward 210 px, 165 px at speed 20. So reach = baseSlashLength x per-stance multiplier, and at the low end the 100 px heavy floor genuinely bites: base 120 at mastery 0 gives 60, clamped up to 100. CAVEAT, stated plainly: the formula line is android v0.682, so under S0-3/C2 it is v0.682 until a web caller is read; what IS web-attested is that the base is an injected per-fighter slash length with a halving branch, not a global constant. Two further web stance cases the original finding did not list: 1t99s0.as:3131 (Dual) = base * 1.4 and :3142 (Reversed) = base * 1.0.

The real count is TWENTY-SIX of 158, and the seven named are simply the first seven in document order. The full list: heavyhorizontalslash_partc (4 empty of 7 frames), balancedhorizontalslash_partc (2/7), balancedjumpslash_parta (2/7), sheathesword (2/7), backstep (2/16), forwardstep (10/16), katanajump (2/4), spearbowjump (2/4), downedup (2/4), downstab_up (7/10), downedup2 (2/25), gangnam (44/88), jutsu_ground_parta (6/9), jutsu_punch_parta (4/5), jutsu_blow_parta (4/8), jutsu_blow_partb (15/18), stomp_parta (5/10), punchcombo_parta (3/5), punchcombo_partb (4/6), punchcombo_partc (3/7), punchcombo_partd (8/12), narutorun (6/12), sheathesword3 (22/33), jutsu_air (5/10), punchground_parta (4/7), punchground_partb (13/16). This enlarges the renderer risk rather than changing its direction: 16% of the human clips contain frames that key NOTHING, and in gangnam and sheathesword3 the empty frames are the majority. A renderer that resets unlisted joints per frame does not merely tear the corpse apart on dismemberment tails - it blanks the character outright for half of two long clips. Carry-forward-last-transform is mandatory, not an optimisation.
